title: Utility Order for Southwestern Electric Power Company, ex parte. — Order No. S-37686 accepts the Staff Report and Recommendation filed on September 11, 2026, which recommends that Rate schedules 71, 72, and 36, of the Request, meets the regulatory requirements as set for in the July 1, 2019 General Order, including the updated Rate Schedule 72 as filed on October 9, 2026. This matter was considered at the October 22, 2026, Business and Executive Session.

LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                                       ORDER NUMBER S-37686

              SOUTHWESTERN ELECTRIC POWER COMPANY, EX PARTE.

Docket No. S-37686, In re: Request for approval of three new proposed rate schedules regarding
curtailable, standby power, and electric vehicle charging services and modification to an
existing rate schedule regarding economic development in accordance with General Order 07-
01-2019 (R-34738).

                 (Decided at the October 22, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)


                                                   ORDER

    I.       OVERVIEW AND PROCEDURAL HISTORY


         On July 23, 2025, Southwestern Electric Power Company (“SWEPCO”) filed a request

that the Louisiana Public Service Commission (“LPSC” or the “Commission”) issue an order

approving of three new proposed rate schedules regarding curtailable, standby power, and electric

vehicle charging services and modification to an existing rate schedule regarding economic

development in accordance with General Order 07-01-2019 (R-34738). (“Request”). Notice of

this proceeding was published in the Commission’s Official Bulletin No. 1355, dated August 1,

2025 for a twenty-five day intervention period. No interventions, timely or otherwise, were filed.

         In the Request, SWEPCO requested Commission approval of three new tariffs and a

modification of an existing tariff. These new tariffs are Rate Schedule 71 Supplementary, Backup,

Maintenance, and As-Available Standby Power Service1, Rate Schedule 72 Curtailable Service

Rider (CSR)2, and Rate Schedule 73 Public Vehicle Charging Facility Service Pilot 3. The

modification is for the existing Rate Schedule 36 Experimental Economic Development Rider

(EDR)4.

         On September 11, 2026, Staff filed its Staff Report and Recommendation (“Staff Report”)

into the record. In this Staff Report, Staff detailed the thorough review of SWEPCO’s Request as



1
  SWEPCO’s request identifies a need for SWEPCO to adjust is tariff based on current market requirements.
SWEPCO identified those requirements where a customer owns and operates its own generation may have a need to
access to power when those generation facilities are not operational or meeting the customer’s current need for
power.
2
  SWEPCO’s request seeks to provides SWEPCO with an additional tool to reduce its system load and enhance its
ability to respond to grid concerns when being asked to by its other market participants. Specifically, SWEPCO
identifies an opportunity for SWEPCO’s customers to voluntarily allow SWEPCO the ability to curtail their service
based on the current needs of SWEPCO’s territory in that region.
3
  SWEPCO’s request seeks to swap the reasoning around its minimum bill calculations as well as additional
adjustment changes. Those changes remove the Wind Asset Rider adjustments if applicable as well as include the
addition of the Storm Recovery Rider if applicable.
4
  SWEPCO’s request for modifications seeks to reduce a threshold for entry for customers of the current Monthly
Base Demand Threshold from 1,000 kW to 500 kW and brings the Billing Credit Factors in alignment with its other
SWEPCO jurisdictions

                                                                                           Order No. S-37686
                                                                                                      Page 1
 well as supporting documentation. Staff recommends that Rate schedules 71, 72, and 36, of the

Request, meets the regulatory requirements as set for in the July 1, 2019 General Order. Staff

further agreed with SWEPCO that the newly proposed tariffs and proposed modifications with

Staff’s edits are reasonable and meet the requirements under the General Order. Staff finds that

SWEPCO should seek approval of Rate Schedule 73 as a part of the existing docket on the matter.

         On October 9, 2026, SWEPCO filed Formal Response to LPSC Staff Report and

Recommendation into the record in which the Company indicated its acceptance of the Staff Report

and Recommendation and provided an update to Tariff Rate Schedule 72, which included updated

curtailable power credit values and clarifying edits. On the same date, Staff filed Formal Response

indicating its review and acceptance of the updated Tariff Rate Schedule 72.



   II.      COMMISSION AUTHORITY
         The Commission exercises jurisdiction in this proceeding pursuant to Article IV, Sec. 21

of the Louisiana Constitution.

         La. Const. Art. IV, Sec. 21 (b) provides in pertinent part:

                 The commission shall regulate all common carriers and public
                 utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided by law.
                 It shall adopt and enforce reasonable rules, regulations and
                 procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties, and shall have
                 other powers and perform other duties as provided by law.


         Pursuant to this authority, the Commission issued its July 1, 2019 General Order, which

set forth rules regarding electric utility tariff fillings and related review. These rules include

Section 501.B:

                 Filings Proposed by an Electric Utility Which Would Result in a
                 Change in Rates – All filings of Rate Schedules or Rate Riders
                 proposed by an Electric utility which would result in a change in
                 Rates shall be filed with the Commission and docketed for
                 consideration. A proposed change in Rate shall be deemed to occur
                 with a proposal for: (1) the addition of new Rate Schedules or Rate
                 Riders; (2) the closing to new Customers of an existing Rate
                 Schedules or Rate Rider; (3) the termination of an existing Rate
                 Schedule or Rate Rider where a Customer is currently taking service
                 under that Rate Schedule or Rate Rider; or (4) the amendment of
                 any existing Rate Schedule or Rate Rider which has the effect of
                 changing Rates. Such filings shall not be considered effectively
                 filed until complying with the minimum requirements identified in
                 Section 401 above, as well as providing an overview of the specific
                 proposed Rate Schedule or Rate Rider submitted for approval.
                 Furthermore, such filing shall not only comply with the Rules
                 contained herein, bust must also comply with the Commissions’
                 Rules of Practice and Procedure, including, but necessarily limited
                 to Rule 13(D)….

                                                                                  Order No. S-37686
                                                                                             Page 2
     III.      STAFF REPORT AND RECOMMENDATION


           LPSC Staff conducted a review of SWEPCO’s Application, current tariffs, and supporting

documentation. SWEPCO’s first requested additional tariff was for the Rate Schedule 71

Supplementary, Backup, Maintenance, and As-Available Standby Power Service identifies a need

for SWEPCO to adjust is tariff based on current market requirements. After review, Staff asserts

this language should be changed to indicate instead of the customer’s own generation should

instead read as the Customer’s interconnected generation that is interconnected into the

Company’s system and are Qualified Facilities within the meaning of Section 201 and 210 of the

Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 and are qualified as such by the Federal Energy

Regulatory Commission (“FERC”).          Staff provided SWEPCO with proposed edits to Rate

Schedule 71.

           SWEPCO’s next requested Tariff was for Rate Schedule 72 Curtailable Service Rider

(CSR) identifies an opportunity for SWEPCO’s customers to voluntarily allow SWEPCO the

ability to curtail their service based on the current needs of SWEPCO’s territory in that region.

Staff believes this optional tariff is a reasonable tool for SWEPCO to utilize. Staff’s belief comes

from recent outage reports that were produced by regulated utilities in front of the LPSC where

the Company highlighted the decision-making guidelines for when the Company is forced to

determine when to shut off a customer’s power due to system load requirements.

           SWEPCO’s request for proposed changes to Rate Schedule 73 Public Electric Vehicle

Charging Facility Service Pilot seek to swap the reasoning around its minimum bill calculations

as well as additional adjustment changes. Due to the fact that there is a pending docket with

intervenors in regard to Rate Schedule 73, Staff recommended that SWEPCO should seek

Commission approval of Rate Schedule 73 as a part of LPSC Docket No. U-36963 and not as a

part of this docket.

           SWEPCO’s final request was for modifications of Rate Schedule 36 Experimental

Economic Development Rider (EDR) seek to reduce a threshold for entry for customers of the

current Monthly Base Demand Threshold from 1,000 kW to 500 kW and brings the Billing Credit

Factors in alignment with its other SWEPCO jurisdictions. Staff agreed with the Company that

the proposed changes lower the barrier for entry into this optional tariff and may produce additional

takers for SWEPCO’s customer base.

                                                                                Order No. S-37686
                                                                                           Page 3
          Staff recommended to the Commission that SWEPCO’s Rate Schedules 71, 72, and 36, of

the Application meets the regulatory requirements as set for in the July 1, 2019 General Order, and

agrees with SWEPCO that the newly proposed tariffs and proposed modifications with Staff’s

edits are reasonable and meet the requirements under the General Order. Staff further

recommended that SWEPCO should seek approval of Rate Schedule 73 as a part of LPSC Docket

No. U-36963. Finally, Staff recommended that SWEPCO comply with the following conditions:

         1. SWEPCO file an updated Tariff with the Utilities Division within 30 days of the

            issuance of an Order in this Docket.

         2. SWEPCO shall make a filing seeking resolution and changes to Rate Schedule 73 in

            Docket U-36963 and not in a separate proceeding.



         On October 9, 2026, SWEPCO filed a Formal Response in which the Company filed its

acceptance of Staff’s Report and Recommendation. The Company further provided an updated

revision to Tariff Schedule 72 with clarifying definitions and minor edits. On the same day, Staff

accepted SWEPCO’s Formal Response.


   IV.      COMMISSION CONSIDERATION

         This matter was considered at the Commission’s October 22, 2026 Business and Executive

Session. After discussion, on motion of Commissioner Campbell, seconded by Chairman

Skrmetta, and unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to accept the Staff Report and

Recommendation filed into the record on September 11, 2026, including the updated Rate

Schedule 72 filed into the record on October 9, 2026.

 IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED THAT:

  1) The Commission accepts the Staff Report and Recommendation filed into the record on
     September 11, 2026, including the updated Rate Schedule 72 as filed on October 9, 2026;
     and
  2) That an order issued in this proceeding be effective immediately.


BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA
